candidates.name: Mississippi Pot Roast Bowls
unmapped_flags: pepperoncini peppers (closest board id is banana-peppers; may be an acceptable sub)
au jus / brown gravy packet
candidates.why: The single most-searched chuck roast recipe in America and not in the catalog. Shreds clean, weighs and divides at 14 servings over mashed potatoes. Source pages report 418-503 cal for meat+gravy alone across variants; over potatoes it lands ~620 with 40g+ protein. Confidence: high on protein, medium on final assembled calorie count (estimated from meat-only nutrition plus a standard potato base).

candidates.name: Classic Slow Cooker Pot Roast with Potatoes and Carrots
candidates.why: The baseline pot roast. Catalog has zero pot roast of any kind despite 55 beef recipes. Everything maps to the board, all-in-one-pot, and the vegetables cook in the same vessel so portioning is a straight weigh-and-divide.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker French Onion Pot Roast Bowls
candidates.why: Distinct flavor lane from plain pot roast (deep caramelized onion plus melted provolone/swiss finish). Slow Cooker French Onion Chicken Bowls already performs in the catalog, so the flavor is proven on the site, but the beef version does not exist. Confidence: medium on calories, estimated from the onion-soup-mix pot roast family.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Balsamic Beef Pot Roast Bowls
candidates.why: Sweet-tangy braise built entirely from pantry staples already on the board. Cheap chuck plus a $2 bottle of balsamic. Slow Cooker Balsamic Pork Bowls is a catalog performer, so the beef counterpart fills an obvious gap. Confidence: medium on calories (estimated from the site's pot roast family).

candidates.name: Horseradish Pot Roast Bowls
unmapped_flags: cream horseradish (board has plain horseradish; close sub)
candidates.why: Verified on the source page at 434 cal / 45g protein for the beef and gravy alone at 8 servings, so with a potato base it clears 600 cal at 45g+ protein. Sharpest protein-to-calorie ratio in the pot roast family and the horseradish gives it a genuinely different mouth than the other braises. Confidence: high, nutrition read directly off the recipe card.

candidates.name: Apple Cider Beef Pot Roast Bowls
unmapped_flags: apple cider (board tracks apple-juice; functionally interchangeable here)
candidates.why: Verified on the source card at 565 cal / 46g protein at 6 servings, vegetables included, so it already meets the bar without any base added. Fall-leaning variant that reads differently from the savory pot roasts. Slow Cooker Apple Cider Pork Bowls exists but the protein is different. Confidence: high, nutrition read off the card.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Swiss Steak with Rice
unmapped_flags: round steak (board covers this as chuck-roast or sirloin-steak; the cheap-cut braise works with either)
candidates.why: Verified at 340 cal / 35g protein for the beef and sauce at 8 servings; over rice it lands near 590 with 38g+ protein. Tomato-braised cheap cut, no cream, no cheese, so it costs almost nothing per serving. Distinct from every existing beef dish in the catalog. Confidence: high.

candidates.name: Beef Manhattan Bowls
unmapped_flags: brown gravy packet (board has jarred-gravy; a packet mix is the cheaper equivalent and is not separately tracked)
candidates.why: Verified at 468 cal / 44g protein for beef and gravy alone at 6 servings; the dish is defined as being served over mashed potatoes, which pushes it near 700 cal at 46g protein. Midwest diner classic, extremely cheap, and the catalog has nothing in the open-faced-roast-beef lane. Confidence: high.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Beef and Noodles
candidates.why: Chuck roast plus egg noodles plus broth, cooked in one vessel, noodles finished in the same pot. About as cheap per serving as beef gets and every ingredient is board-tracked. Distinct from the existing Ground Beef Stroganoff Pasta because there is no dairy and the beef is shredded whole-muscle. Confidence: medium on calories, estimated from the ingredient set.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Beef Tips and Gravy over Mashed Potatoes
candidates.why: Sirloin tips or cubed chuck in a from-scratch pan gravy over potatoes. Enormously popular search term, nothing like it in the catalog (Salisbury Steak and Potato Bowls is a ground beef patty dish). Scales to 14 servings without any change in technique. Confidence: medium on calories.

candidates.name: Classic Beef Stew with Potatoes and Carrots
candidates.why: The catalog has 55 beef recipes and not one plain beef stew, which is the most-cooked cheap-beef dinner in the country. Fully board-mappable, freezes and reheats better than almost anything else in the run, and the potato load carries it over 500 cal on its own. Confidence: medium-high.

candidates.name: Irish Beef and Guinness Stew
unmapped_flags: Guinness / stout beer (no board id; beef-broth plus a splash of balsamic is the non-alcoholic sub if needed)
candidates.why: Deeper and maltier than plain beef stew, with bacon adding fat and flavor for pennies. Clearly separable from the classic stew on the plate and in the write-up. The only ingredient off the board is the stout, which is one cheap can per batch. Confidence: medium-high on calories.

candidates.name: Beef Bourguignon Bowls
unmapped_flags: dry red wine (no board id)
pearl onions (board has onions; quartered yellow onion is the standard cheap sub)
candidates.why: The French benchmark braise, and the mushroom-bacon-wine profile is genuinely distinct from the American stews. Chuck is the correct cut, which keeps it cheap despite the fancy name. Confidence: medium on calories, estimated over a potato or noodle base.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Sauerbraten Bowls
unmapped_flags: gingersnap cookies (used as the gravy thickener; board tracks cookies generically but not gingersnaps)
candidates.why: Verified at 295 cal / 23g protein for the meat and gravy at 8 servings from a 2 lb roast; our 14-serving build raises the meat ratio and adds potatoes, landing around 560 cal at 35g+ protein. Sweet-sour German braise is a lane the catalog has never touched. Confidence: medium, the source portions less beef per serving than we will.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Chuck Roast Stroganoff over Egg Noodles
candidates.why: Whole-muscle slow-braised version of stroganoff, shredded rather than crumbled. Confidence: NEAR-DUPE RISK, flagging for the selector. Ground Beef Stroganoff Pasta and One-Pot Ground Turkey Stroganoff are both live; this is the same sauce with a different beef format. Include only if the selector judges the chuck version distinct enough.

candidates.name: Cottage Pie
candidates.why: One of the biggest gaps in the catalog: no shepherd's or cottage pie exists at all despite it being a top-tier cheap family dinner. Bakes in a sheet pan or two, cuts into equal squares, so 14-serving portioning is trivially exact. Independent sources report 30-39g protein per serving. Confidence: high.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Beef and Potato Au Gratin Casserole
candidates.why: Verified on the card at 556 cal / 35g protein per serving at 6 servings, so it clears the bar as written with no adjustment. Seven cheap board ingredients total and it layers rather than assembles, which is ideal for batch. Confidence: high, nutrition read off the recipe card.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker BBQ Shredded Beef Bowls
candidates.why: The catalog has BBQ Pulled Pork Rice Bowl and Slow Cooker BBQ Pulled Chicken Bowls but no beef version, which is the obvious third leg. Five-ingredient braise, everything board-tracked, shreds and weighs out cleanly. Confidence: medium on calories.

candidates.name: Corned Beef and Cabbage Dinner Bowls
unmapped_flags: corned beef brisket (NO BOARD ID; board tracks corned-beef-hash canned only. Signature ingredient is unmapped, so this needs a price home before it can be costed)
candidates.why: Genuine one-pot dinner that hits 40g+ protein, and corned beef goes on deep discount every March. Flagging the main ingredient: the board has no corned beef brisket commodity, so this cannot be priced today. Include only if a commodity gets registered, otherwise hold. Confidence: medium on calories.

candidates.name: Honey Garlic Steak Bites and Potatoes
candidates.why: Sirloin cubed and braised or seared in bulk, then tossed in a honey-garlic glaze and served over potatoes. Steak bites are a whole popular category the catalog has zero of. Slow Cooker Honey Garlic Pork Bowls exists but the protein and format differ. Confidence: medium on calories.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Steak and Onions over Rice
unmapped_flags: Italian dressing seasoning mix and brown gravy mix packets (board tracks italian-dressing and jarred-gravy, not the dry packets)
candidates.why: Verified at 341 cal / 31g protein for the beef and gravy at 6 servings; over rice it lands near 580 at 34g protein. Uses the cheapest petite sirloins in the case, which is exactly the cut the board prices well. Confidence: high on the meat nutrition, medium on the assembled bowl.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Cube Steak and Gravy Bowls
unmapped_flags: cube steak (tenderized round; no board id, closest is chuck-roast or sirloin-steak)
candidates.why: Cheapest beef cut in the meat case, braised until fork-tender in gravy. Confidence: NEAR-DUPE RISK flagged for the selector against the live Salisbury Steak and Potato Bowls, which is the same gravy-over-potatoes idea with a ground patty instead of whole muscle. Also carries an unmapped cut. Lowest-priority candidate in this slice.

candidates.name: Beef Birria Rice Bowls
unmapped_flags: dried guajillo chiles
dried ancho chiles
dried arbol chiles (none of the three dried chiles have board ids; enchilada-sauce is the closest tracked shortcut)
candidates.why: Birria is the highest-demand Mexican beef dish of the last five years and the catalog has none. The live Slow Cooker Barbacoa Burrito Bowl is a different braise (adobo and chipotle, no chile-consomme base), so it should survive dedup. Flagging that the signature dried chiles have no board home. Confidence: medium on calories, estimated over a rice base.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Chile Colorado Bowls
unmapped_flags: dried New Mexico / guajillo / ancho chiles (no board id; enchilada-sauce is the tracked shortcut)
candidates.why: Beef stewed in pure red chile sauce, no beans, no tomato. Different enough from birria (no consomme, no vinegar-clove profile) and from the existing enchilada skillet (ground beef, canned sauce). Chuck is the correct and cheapest cut. Confidence: medium on calories.

candidates.name: Carne Guisada (Tex-Mex Beef and Potato Stew)
candidates.why: Every ingredient maps to the board with nothing exotic, and the potatoes push it past 500 cal without a separate base. Fills the Tex-Mex braise gap: the catalog's Tex-Mex beef entries are all ground beef skillets. Thickens into its own gravy so it holds up in containers. Confidence: medium-high.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Beef Tinga Bowls
candidates.why: Smoky chipotle-tomato shredded beef, fully board-mappable (chipotle-adobo is tracked). The catalog has chicken tinga and pork tinga but no beef tinga, which is the obvious third. Three-ingredient sauce keeps the cost per serving low. Confidence: medium on calories.

candidates.name: Steak Fajita Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Catalog has Fajita Chicken Rice Bowl and Ground Turkey Fajita Rice Bowls but no beef fajita bowl, which is the version most people actually order. Sirloin sliced thin and seared in batches scales fine to 14 servings. Everything is on the board. Confidence: medium.

candidates.name: Slow Cooker Carne Asada Rice Bowls
candidates.why: The slow cooker version solves the batch problem that kills grilled carne asada: no fry-to-order step, it braises in the citrus marinade and shreds. Distinct from barbacoa (citrus-forward, no chipotle) and from the existing burrito bowls. Confidence: medium on calories.

candidates.name: Ropa Vieja Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Cuba's national dish and a natural companion to the live Cuban Beef Picadillo Rice Bowls without duplicating it (shredded whole muscle with peppers and olives vs ground beef with raisins). Chuck substitutes for flank at a third the cost. Source pages report 26-39g protein for the meat alone. Confidence: medium-high.

candidates.name: Salsa Verde Beef Bowls
candidates.why: Verified at 346 cal / 33g protein for the beef at 8 servings; over rice and beans it lands near 570 at 38g protein. Four-ingredient dump recipe, everything board-tracked including poblano-peppers. The catalog has chicken and pork chile verde but no beef. Confidence: high on the meat nutrition.

candidates.name: Shredded Beef Chili con Carne Bowls
candidates.why: Texas-style chili built on cubed chuck that shreds, not ground beef. Confidence: NEAR-DUPE RISK flagged for the selector against Beef Chili Rice Bowls and Beef Chili Mac, both of which are ground beef. The whole-muscle texture is the entire point of the dish, but the selector should judge whether that is enough separation.

candidates.name: Carne en su Jugo Bowls
unmapped_flags: serrano peppers (board tracks jalapenos, a workable sub)
candidates.why: Verified on the card at 620 cal / 58g protein per serving at 6 servings, the single highest protein density in this slice, and it needs no rice base to get there. Jalisco classic that nobody on the site has seen. Tomatillos are board-tracked. Confidence: high, nutrition read off the recipe card.

candidates.name: Hungarian Beef Goulash
unmapped_flags: caraway seeds (no board id; optional)
candidates.why: The real gulyas, which is a paprika beef braise with potatoes, not the American macaroni skillet. The live American Goulash Pasta is a completely different dish, so this is not a dupe despite the shared name, and the write-up can make that distinction the hook. Paprika is board-tracked. Confidence: medium-high.

candidates.name: Greek Stifado (Beef and Onion Stew)
unmapped_flags: pearl onions (board has onions; quartered yellow onion is the standard cheap substitution)
red wine (optional, vinegar carries the acid)
candidates.why: Verified at 467 cal / 56g protein per serving at 5 servings on the source card, before any base is added. Cinnamon-and-clove sweet-sour braise is unlike anything in the catalog, and the Greek slot currently only holds Pastitsio and Greek Beef and Chickpea Bowls. Confidence: high on nutrition.

candidates.name: Moussaka (Greek Beef and Eggplant Bake)
unmapped_flags: eggplant (no board id; the potato-only version is a legitimate variant if eggplant cannot be priced)
candidates.why: Layered bake, cuts into exact squares, so 14 servings portions perfectly. Greek comfort-food benchmark and the bechamel top gives it a completely different mouth than Pastitsio (pasta) which is the only comparable live dish. Flagging eggplant as unpriceable today. Confidence: medium on calories.

candidates.name: Moroccan Beef Tagine with Chickpeas
unmapped_flags: dried apricots (no board id)
dates (no board id; both are optional sweeteners, honey works)
candidates.why: Verified on the card at roughly 700 cal / 65g protein at 4 servings, so it clears the bar with enormous headroom. Chickpeas stretch the beef and are board-tracked, which makes this one of the cheapest per-serving candidates in the slice. Catalog has chicken tagine but no beef. Confidence: high on nutrition.

candidates.name: Ethiopian Key Wat (Berbere Beef Stew) Bowls
candidates.why: berbere-seasoning is already a board commodity because of the live Ethiopian Doro Wat Chicken Bowls, so the beef counterpart costs out immediately. Enormous onion base means the beef stretches far. Confidence: LOW on the source page's stated nutrition, which reads 137 cal / 2g protein for a stew built on 1.5 lb of beef and is obviously a broken auto-calculation. My estimate is built from the ingredient list instead, not the card.

candidates.name: Beef Rendang Rice Bowls
unmapped_flags: kaffir lime leaves (optional)
galangal (fresh-ginger is the standard sub)
candidates.why: The catalog has Malaysian Chicken Rendang but beef is the canonical rendang, and lemongrass-paste plus coconut-milk-canned are both already board commodities. Cooks down to a dry-ish curry that holds beautifully in containers for a week. Confidence: medium on calories.

candidates.name: Massaman Beef Curry with Potatoes
unmapped_flags: massaman curry paste (board tracks red-curry-paste; massaman is the closest untracked variant, red paste plus cinnamon and cardamom is the working sub)
candidates.why: The one Thai curry built for cheap braising cuts rather than quick-cooking protein, so chuck is correct here. Peanuts and potatoes are both board-tracked and push it well over 500 cal. Catalog Thai entries are all chicken, turkey or ground beef. Confidence: medium.

candidates.name: Beef Vindaloo Rice Bowls
unmapped_flags: dried Kashmiri chiles (cayenne-pepper plus paprika is the tracked sub)
candidates.why: Vinegar-forward Goan braise, sharply different from the two live keema curries which are both ground and pea-based. Every spice in it is already a board commodity thanks to the Indian chicken recipes. Chuck is the right cut. Confidence: medium on calories.

candidates.name: Taiwanese Braised Beef Noodle Bowls
unmapped_flags: doubanjiang / chili bean paste (gochujang or chili-crisp are the tracked near-subs)
star anise (no board id)
Shaoxing wine (optional)
candidates.why: Taiwan's national dish and a genuine noodle bowl rather than a thin soup, so it carries the calories. Chuck is explicitly the recommended cut. Distinct from Beef Chow Mein (ground beef stir-fry) in every respect. Confidence: medium on calories.

candidates.name: Vietnamese Bo Kho (Lemongrass Beef Stew)
unmapped_flags: star anise (no board id)
annatto oil (paprika is the standard color sub)
candidates.why: Aromatic beef stew over rice noodles, both lemongrass-paste and rice-noodles already on the board. The live Vietnamese beef entry is a caramelized ground beef bowl, so there is no overlap. Chuck or shank both work; chuck keeps it cheap. Confidence: medium.

candidates.name: Gyudon (Japanese Beef and Onion Rice Bowls)
unmapped_flags: dashi (chicken-broth or beef-broth is the working sub)
candidates.why: Thinly sliced beef simmered with onions over rice. Cheapest possible Japanese beef dish because the meat is sliced paper-thin, which stretches a small amount a long way, and mirin is a board commodity. Distinct from Japanese Ground Beef Curry and from Loco Moco. Confidence: medium on calories with a soft-egg topper.

candidates.name: Beef Bulgogi Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Sliced marinated beef, grated pear in the marinade, seared in batches. Confidence: NEAR-DUPE RISK flagged for the selector against the live Korean Ground Beef Rice Bowls, which uses the same soy-brown-sugar-sesame base with crumbled beef. Bulgogi's pear marinade and sliced texture are the differentiators. Selector's call.

candidates.name: Pepper Steak with Rice
candidates.why: Every single ingredient is board-tracked, no exceptions, which makes it one of the cleanest costings in the slice. Takeout staple with nothing comparable in the catalog (the live beef-and-pepper dishes are all Philly cheesesteak or unstuffed pepper formats). Sears in batches for 14 servings. Confidence: medium-high.

candidates.name: Beef in Black Bean Sauce Rice Bowls
unmapped_flags: fermented black beans or jarred black bean garlic sauce (no board id; canned-black-beans is NOT a substitute, this is a different product)
candidates.why: Deeply savory takeout dish the catalog has no version of, and oyster-sauce plus soy-sauce are both board commodities. Flagging clearly that the namesake ingredient is unmapped and cannot be faked with canned black beans. Confidence: medium on calories.

candidates.name: Chinese Beef with Honey Black Pepper Sauce
candidates.why: Fully board-mappable, punchy peppery-sweet glaze that is distinct from teriyaki and from the honey-garlic lane. Velveting with cornstarch means cheap sirloin comes out tender, which is exactly the budget angle. Confidence: medium.

candidates.name: Vietnamese Shaking Beef Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Bo luc lac, cubed seared sirloin with a lime-pepper dipping sauce. Everything maps to the board, cubes sear in batches without any per-plate assembly, and it is nothing like the live caramelized ground beef bowl. Confidence: medium on calories over rice.

candidates.name: Filipino Beef Caldereta
unmapped_flags: liver spread (peanut-butter is the accepted board-tracked substitution and is already in most modern versions)
candidates.why: The catalog is strong on Filipino pork and chicken (adobo, tinga, giniling, inasal, afritada) but has no Filipino beef dish at all. Peanut butter and cheese in the sauce make it distinctive, potatoes and carrots carry the calories, and chuck is the recommended cut. Confidence: medium.

candidates.name: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
unmapped_flags: aji amarillo paste (no board id; a mild chili paste or harissa-paste thinned down is the closest tracked option)
candidates.why: Source card reads 921 cal / 22g protein using beef tenderloin at 4 servings; our build swaps to sirloin and raises the meat ratio, landing near 700 cal at 40g+ protein. Rice AND fries in the same bowl is the whole identity of the dish, so calories are never in question. No South American beef dish exists in the catalog.
